Article Title: 'Whenever you see me calm on the court and I'm losing, it could be because I don't care': Daniil Medvedev on why emotions matter
Article Text:
Daniil Medvedev (AP Photo)

Excerpts:

You’ve had a consistent run this year, after struggling last year, what was the difference?

Do you see

Alexander Zverev

’s success, and your own form this year, as something that gives hope to the locker room?

You’re analytical and clear-headed by nature, but what happens when you’re caught in the heat of a match?

You changed the way you celebrated after matches six-seven years ago, do you think you would be able to do that during matches, change the way you react?

Do you think if you were calmer, you would be a better competitor?

Would you back yourself to win a

Grand Slam title

next year?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

“Improving is key for Dhamne”

ALMATY: After slipping to No. 18 last September -- his lowest ranking in seven years -- former world No. 1 Daniil Medvedev has mounted a determined resurgence in 2026, climbing back to No. 5. The top seed at the Almaty Open, the 30-year-old is making a late-season push to secure his place at the ATP Finals in November.In tennis there can be a lot of reasons, so I will not be able to tell you any one reason. I'm happy that I managed to make a better year this year than last year. I enjoyed a lot of parts of this year, and, if I can be in Turin, that's going to be a great bonus to having a good year.There have been injuries, as you saw, with Jannik (Sinner), and Carlos (Alcaraz), they were champions at Grand Slams for some time, but when one is injured, there is only one left and once both of them are injured this is an opportunity for someone else.Sasha (Zverev) had a tremendous year, super consistent, because even if you look at his matches in the last tournament in Shanghai, he probably was not playing his best level still he made the semis of a Masters 1000.So that's how strong he was this year.A lot of emotions, adrenalin come into play when you are trying to win, it changes your reaction to circumstances. Tennis players react in different ways, maybe some blame themselves without saying it out loudly… As I like to say, we're all a bit crazy. It's just that when someone is crazy he starts to scream, and when another is crazy, he maybe goes to the hotel room after and breaks everything there. I don't go crazy in the hotel room, but if something happens in the heat of the moment, sometimes I don't control my emotions as I would like to. But again, it is something I've been working on and I've made progress.With the celebrations it is super easy, because it's not every match that you win 7-6, in the third. So if it is, like 5-4, 40-15, you basically know before the point that if you make an ace the match is over, you won the match. So I don't have this rush of emotions, like when I beat Arthur Fils in a tough match, a tough moment in my career, in my season. It was a shot that he should have made and he missed it. During this moment, I had a rush of adrenalin like, wow, I won. I didn't expect it.For me, sometimes it happens, let's say I'm losing 5-2, the guy is serving, and it's 40-love, and he wins a point. Then maybe he doesn't fall down, but he looks at his team and celebrates for 30 seconds. I don't like it. I feel like shake my hand and then celebrate. So, I try to do more like this.It would take away from me. Whenever you see me calm on the court and I'm losing, it could be because I don't care at this moment for many different reasons. I could have just had a bad day, it happens because we play 100 matches a year. Most of the time, I want to win, that's why I react the way I react. I have to be calmer sometimes, also to be able to overcome obstacles during the match, but that's something during my career I was able to do. Most of the time though, I should be who I am.Jannik (Sinner) if he's healthy, Carlos (Acaraz) or Sasha (Zverev), at this point should be, but I believe in myself. I believe I can do much better than I did the last two years in Slams. I believe I'm proving it in the other tournaments and I know how to do it in general. I have experience of playing good in Slams. So it's just about collecting the good things from the other tournaments, putting them in the Grand Slam week, be able to do it for two weeks, and, again, I know I can do it.Daniil Medvedev believes Manas Dhamne is on the right track, with the former world No. 1 stressing that steady improvement is what matters most for the 18-year-old Indian, currently ranked No. 393.“Once you drop in the rankings or stay at the same ranking, it can get a bit tough, especially when you're a junior,” Medvedev said. “So it's always about a tiny bit of improvement. I feel like, from what I see from him, he is. That's the most important thing. He's a good player.”The Russian pointed to the unpredictable nature of the development of a young player, citing Spaniard Rafael Jodar as an example. Jodar began the season ranked No. 165 and has surged to No. 11 this week, underlining how quickly a player's fortunes can change.“If you asked me about Jodar last year, I would say, great player, can be top 100, top 50, top 10, but you never know,” Medvedev said. “This is up to many, many things. Let's see if he's (Dhamne) able to do it.”
Article Summary: Former world No. 1 Daniil Medvedev is the top seed at the Almaty Open. The 30-year-old is making a late-season push to secure his place at the ATP Finals. "I'm happy that I managed to make a better year this year than last year," he says. "Tennis players react in different ways, maybe some blame themselves"

Article Title: Sheetal Devi strikes double gold again! Indian archer repeats 2023 Asian Para Games medal feat in 2026
Article Text:
Indian para-archer Sheetal Devi wins three Asian Para Games medals again.

Sheetal turns the tide to defend individual crown

Three medals again, just like Hangzhou

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Indian para-archer Sheetal Devi once again proved her mettle on the biggest continental stage, winning two gold medals at the Asian Para Games for the second consecutive edition after clinching the women's individual compound title on Thursday.The 19-year-old armless archer from Jammu and Kashmir produced a stunning comeback to defeat Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah 142-139 in the final at Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Multipurpose Square, successfully defending the individual title she won in Hangzhou in 2023.The victory completed a memorable double-gold day for Sheetal, who had teamed up with Toman Kumar to win the compound mixed team gold earlier in the day. She also secured a silver medal in the women's compound doubles event alongside Odisha's quadruple amputee archer Payal Nag.With three medals — two golds and a silver — Sheetal has replicated her medal tally from the 2023 Asian Para Games, where she also won two gold medals and a silver to announce herself as one of India's brightest para-sporting talents.Sheetal had to dig deep to retain her individual crown, with Alim initially putting the Indian under pressure in their gold medal clash.The Singaporean archer established a four-point advantage after the opening two ends, leaving Sheetal with plenty of work to do. However, the Indian mounted an extraordinary recovery, firing six 10s, including three Xs — arrows landing closest to the centre of the target — across the next two ends.The remarkable sequence helped Sheetal overturn the deficit and take a two-point lead into the final end, setting up a tense finish.With the gold medal on the line, Sheetal maintained her composure, scoring three 9s for 27 points in the final end. Alim, meanwhile, managed scores of 9, 8 and 9 for 26 points, allowing the Indian to seal a 142-139 victory.The triumph was particularly significant as it came less than a couple of hours after Sheetal had won the mixed team gold with Toman, underlining her ability to deliver under pressure across multiple events.Sheetal's campaign in 2026 has followed a familiar pattern from her breakthrough performance at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, China.At the previous edition, she won gold in the women's individual compound event and the compound mixed team competition alongside Rakesh Kumar. She also claimed silver in the women's team event with Sarita.Three years later, Sheetal repeated that medal-winning feat, this time collecting individual and mixed team gold medals alongside a silver with Payal Nag in the women's compound doubles.The Indian duo had topped the ranking round in the doubles event but lost 141-150 to China's Xueqing Xu and Jing Zhao in the final on Wednesday.Sheetal's latest triumph further strengthens her reputation as a leading figure in Indian para-archery. Having already made history in Hangzhou by becoming the first Indian woman to win two gold medals in a single edition of the Asian Para Games, she has now successfully repeated the feat in 2026.At just 19, Sheetal continues to turn extraordinary personal determination into landmark sporting achievements, delivering another golden chapter for India on the para-sporting stage.
Article Summary: Indian para-archer Sheetal Devi wins three Asian Para Games medals again. 19-year-old armless archer from Jammu and Kashmir produced a stunning comeback to defeat Singapore's Alim Nur Syahidah 142-139 in the final. She also secured a silver medal in the women's compound doubles event alongside Odisha's quadruple amputee archer Payal Nag.

Article Title: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt handed two-match ban for medication breach
Article Text:
Australia's Megan Schutt (PTI Photo)

Cricket Australia clarifies nature of breach

Schutt accepts sanction and apologises

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Suspension follows impressive ODI series

Poll Vote & Share your view What impact will Schutt's absence have on the Australian T20I team? Severe impact, they will struggle. Minimal impact, they have depth. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt has been handed a two-match suspension for failing to comply with requirements governing the use of prescription medication, Cricket Australia (CA) said on Thursday.The 33-year-old will miss Australia's third and final T20I against New Zealand at North Sydney Oval on Thursday, as well as Adelaide Strikers' opening match of the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL) against Melbourne Stars on October 31.Cricket Australia clarified that the breach involved a single incident that occurred outside competition and was not related to performance enhancement. The suspension applies to both international and domestic cricket.In a statement, CA said the offence involved non-compliance with its medical guidelines governing prescription medication."The breach was a failure to adhere to requirements under the Sports Science and Sports Medicine guidelines with regard to prescription medication," Cricket Australia said.The governing body also stressed that the incident was isolated and had occurred outside the competitive environment."This (breach) relates to a single incidence which occurred while out of competition and was not for performance enhancing purposes," CA added.The suspension means Schutt will be unavailable for Australia's series-deciding T20I against New Zealand and will also miss the beginning of her domestic campaign with Adelaide Strikers.Schutt accepted the suspension and apologised for not meeting the standards expected of players representing Australian cricket."I fully accept the penalty handed down and apologise for failing to meet the standards expected of me. I'm sorry for the attention this has caused and appreciate the support I've received," Schutt said in her statement.The fast bowler acknowledged that players were regularly educated about the relevant guidelines and accepted responsibility for complying with them."While this occurred out of competition and was not performance related, I understand that I am responsible for following the Sports Science and Sports Medicine Guidelines, which players receive regular education on, and I should have adhered to these guidelines," she added.CA said it would continue to provide appropriate support to Schutt while reinforcing the standards and responsibilities expected of everyone representing the game.The ban comes after Schutt enjoyed an outstanding ODI series against Bangladesh, finishing as Player of the Series after taking 10 wickets at an average of 7.1.Her absence is a setback for Australia ahead of the final T20I against New Zealand, while Adelaide Strikers will also have to manage without the experienced pacer for their WBBL opener.The suspension is limited to two matches, with CA's statement making clear that the incident was not related to performance-enhancing purposes.
Article Summary: Australia fast bowler Megan Schutt handed two-match suspension. Schutt failed to comply with requirements governing the use of prescription medication. The 33-year-old will miss Australia's third and final T20I against New Zealand. She will also miss Adelaide Strikers' opening match of the Women's Big Bash League (WBBL)

Article Title: Asian Para Games: Simran Sharma, Praveen Kumar and Sachin Khilari lead India’s athletics gold rush
Article Text:
Simran Sharma (Image credit: PCI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Image credit: PCI

Simran Sharma’s golden double headlined India’s athletics campaign on Day 3 of the Asian Para Games, as track and field athletes collected 22 medals, including five gold, in Nagoya on Wednesday.After winning the women’s 200m T12 title on Tuesday, the visually impaired sprinter claimed the 100m gold in a Gamesrecord 12.02 seconds, ahead of Iran’s Hajar Safarzadeh (12.30). Simran became only the fourth Indian to win two gold medals at a single Para Asiad, joining Ankur Dhama, Sheetal Devi and Nishad Kumar.Dilip Gavit supplied another track gold, winning the men’s 100m T46/47 combined event in 10.69s. Mohammed Basil Morssinganakathi, competing in T47, took silver in a Games-record 10.72s. T46 and T47 cover athletes with upperlimb impairments, differing in the nature and extent of the impairment.Field events brought three more gold. Ayush Verma topped the men’s shot put F53 with 8.16m. The class is for seated throwers with significant trunk and leg movement impairments. Praveen Kumar defended his men’s high jump T44/64 title, clearing a Games-record 2.05m. Praveen has a lower-limb impairment -- T64 athletes use a prosthesis, while T44 covers lower-limb impairments without one.Banti claimed silver with a personal best 1.92m in the same event.Sachin Khilari completed the gold rush with a Games-record 15.87m in the men’s shot put F46, securing a podium sweep for India. Mohd Yasser won the silver at 15.06m and Parveen took the bronze at 14.94m.Other silver came from Bhagyashri Jadhav (women’s shot put F34, personal best 8.19m), Manjeet (men’s javelin F12/13, career-best 61.03m), Preeti Pal (women’s 100m T35), Akira Banothu (men’s 400m T35/38) and Sharath Makanahalli, whose men’s 1500m T12 medal after Uzbekistan’s winner was disqualified for obstruction.India’s athletics tally has risen to 42 medals, 13 gold, 14 silver and 15 bronze, second only to China. Athletics has so far accounted for 13 of India’s 14 gold medals across all sports at the Games.
Article Summary: Simran Sharma becomes fourth Indian to win two gold medals at a single Para Asiad. India's athletics tally has risen to 42 medals, 13 gold, 14 silver and 15 bronze. Athletics has so far accounted for 13 of India’s 14 gold medals across all sports at the Games.

Article Title: UCL round-up: Como humiliate Manchester United; Real Madrid maintain perfect record
Article Text:
Michael Carrick (AP Photo)

Como dominate after the break

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Real Madrid win, Bayern and Arsenal draw

Como produced an impressive 4-1 win over Manchester United on Matchday 3 of the UEFA Champions League 2026-27 at Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia on Wednesday.Argentine playmaker Nico Paz scored twice as Cesc Fabregas’s side dominated the match and handed United their second consecutive defeat in the competition.Como got off to a flying start when Paz scored in the second minute. He took advantage of a mistake in midfield before firing a left-footed shot into the net. Manchester United tried to fight back, but Como’s organised defence kept the visitors from creating clear chances before half-time.Como strengthened their grip on the match just four minutes into the second half. Tasos Douvikas finished a quick attack down the right flank in the 49th minute to make it 2-0.Paz struck again in the 57th minute, finishing calmly from the edge of the penalty area after a swift counter-attack. His second goal put Como in a commanding position, with Michael Carrick's side struggling to cope with the hosts’ attacking threat.The Italian side added a fourth goal in the 75th minute when Jacobo Ramon headed home from a well-delivered corner. Manchester United managed to score a consolation goal in stoppage time, with substitute Joshua Zirkzee converting a low cross from Amad Diallo in the 90+1st minute.However, the late goal could not change the result. Paz emerged as the star of the night, with his two goals helping Como take full advantage of United’s defensive weaknesses.The result marked an important European victory for Como, while Manchester United were left to reflect on their second straight Champions League defeat.Elsewhere, Real Madrid beat Leipzig 4-1 to maintain their perfect record in the league phase. Bayern Munich and Arsenal played out a 2-2 draw, while Inter Milan secured a narrow 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk.Aston Villa defeated Viking 3-1, Club Brugge beat Lens 3-0, and LASK edged Sporting CP 3-2. Real Betis also claimed a 1-0 victory over Feyenoord.
Article Summary: Como beat Manchester United 4-1 on Matchday 3 of the UEFA Champions League 2026-27. Nico Paz scored twice as Cesc Fabregas' side dominated the match. Manchester United suffered their second consecutive defeat in the competition. Bayern Munich and Arsenal played out a 2-2 draw. Inter Milan secured a narrow 1-0 win over Shakhtar Donetsk.

Article Title: EFI administrator seeks Rs 25 lakh in damages, serves defamation notice on Hangzhou Asiad gold medallist Chheda
Article Text:
India’s Hriday Vipul Chheda (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

New Delhi: In a bizarre turn of events, Lt Col Sandeep Dewan, member (administration) of the ad hoc committee governing the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), has served a defamation notice on Hangzhou Asian Games gold medallist Hriday Chheda, demanding Rs 25 lakh in damages and an unconditional apology over allegations concerning the handling of the Indian dressage team ahead of and during the recently concluded Aichi-Nagoya multisport continental event.The six-page legal notice, dated October 17 and in possession of TOI, also seeks the withdrawal and deletion of Chheda’s September 8 email to the Indian Olympic Association (IOA) and sports officials, in which the rider alleged that the veterinary report declaring his horse, Dono Di Maggio, unfit was engineered to clear the way for reserve Anush Agarwalla. Chheda accused Dewan of collusion, fraud and concealment, questioning the attempt to jeopardise his participation in the Asian Games.The development raises questions over the priorities of an administrator appointed to restore order in a federation long plagued by governance controversies, internal power struggles and selection disputes. Instead of addressing an athlete’s grievances, the administrator is now seeking damages from one of India’s leading riders for raising concerns about his conduct.For the record, Chheda’s horse, Dono Di Maggio, was subsequently cleared by the Games organisers to compete in Japan.The horse was the best-performing among the Indian riders in Aichi-Nagoya.After being served the notice, Chheda expressed deep anguish over the way he had been treated and wrote a strongly worded email to IOA president P T Usha."The vindictiveness, high-handedness and arrogance is apparent from the attached legal notice. The irony is appalling: an athlete who faced harassment and an attempt to prevent his participation and subsequently demonstrated through his horse’s performances that he was fit to compete, is now facing legal threats from the very person whose conduct he questioned," Chheda wrote to Usha. The email is in possession of TOI."An administration that resorts to legal threats against athletes rather than welcoming scrutiny of its own conduct has no place in sporting governance. Individuals such as Col Dewan must be held accountable for their conduct and questioned on their suitability to hold positions of responsibility in Indian sport," Chheda said."Meanwhile, athletes have received no meaningful support from the Federation and continue to bear the consequences of its failures. The multiple legal disputes concerning the Federation’s functioning, along with the reported suspension by the international governing body, FEI, have further jeopardised athletes’ careers and international participation," he added.Dewan’s notice, however, disputed the allegations, maintaining that the veterinary examination covered all Indian team horses and that the decision on a late replacement rested with the IOA, not with him individually. It stated that the September 8 email falsely accused him of fraud, collusion and concealment, thereby damaging his reputation."The impugned email has gravely harmed my client's reputation as a veteran Army officer, as a sports administrator and as Team Leader. It has exposed him to suspicion and ridicule among the very persons with whom he must work and caused him severe mental distress," Dewan's lawyer, Aroon Menon, stated in the notice issued on his client's behalf."By making and publishing the impugned email, you have committed the offence of defamation under Section 356(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, punishable under Section 356(2). My client is the person aggrieved and is entitled to file a complaint under Section 222 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023. Your acts also constitute the civil wrong of libel, for which my client is entitled to sue you for damages, a mandatory injunction directing retraction and a permanent injunction restraining further publication," the lawyer stated."You are therefore called upon within 7 (seven) days of receipt of this notice to: (i) Unconditionally withdraw the impugned email and every imputation in it against my client; (ii) Tender an unconditional written apology to my client, sent by email from hridaychheda98@gmail.com to every recipient of the impugned email, with a copy to the undersigned; (iii) Delete the impugned email and refrain from forwarding, circulating or repeating it or any similar imputation, in any medium, including email, messaging apps, social media and the press; (iv) Pay an amount of Rs 25,00,000 (twenty-five lakh) as compensation to my client for the harm to his reputation and the mental distress caused, and Rs 50,000 (fifty thousand) towards the costs of the present notice," the notice added.
Article Summary: Lt Col Sandeep Dewan served a defamation notice on Hriday Chheda. Dewan is a member of the ad hoc committee governing the Equestrian Federation of India. He is demanding Rs 25 lakh in damages and an unconditional apology. The six-page legal notice, dated October 17, is in possession of TOI.

Article Title: 'I try to emulate his technique': Temba Bavuma reveals Sachin Tendulkar influence after career-best 179
Article Text:
Sachin Tendulkar and Temba Bavuma (Agency Image)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

South Africa captain Temba Bavuma has revealed how batting great Sachin Tendulkar has influenced his technique, explaining how he has tried to adapt the Indian legend's approach to suit his own game.Bavuma made the admission after scoring a career-best 179 against Australia in the second Test at St George's Park, helping South Africa recover from 110/6 to post 425/9 declared.Asked about the similarities between his technique and that of Tendulkar, one of his heroes, Bavuma said he had consciously tried to incorporate aspects of the former India batter's approach, particularly his movement and ability to play the ball close to his body."Yeah, I mean, I try to emulate my technique to his. I mean, I'm obviously not a big guy. I'm not really going to get any big strides in. I try to be efficient in terms of my movement. Sometimes it gets me into trouble. But I think for me, that's generally what works. I try to play the ball as close to my body as possible," Bavuma said.The South African skipper's 179, which came off 334 balls, was his highest Test score, surpassing his previous best of 172 against the West Indies in 2023. He admitted that the innings was particularly satisfying given his recent struggles to find rhythm."Yeah, definitely one of my better ones. I think looking at the situation of the game, and I think personally as well, I found myself a lot in those type of situations, coming in early, trying to manage myself to kind of scramble through to a 50 or 60, but I think what was nice and the ability just to take it even further and make it count," he said.Bavuma also spoke about the challenge of facing Australia's formidable bowling attack, which includes several highly ranked Test bowlers. Having failed to make a significant contribution in the first Test, he was keen to make amends."So, I mean, we got a taste of it in the first Test, and we kind of knew what was up for us. So I think for me, obviously not being able to contribute from the first Test and then coming in here in the second Test, I think that was a big thing on my mind. But yeah, I was glad I was able to put in a good contribution for the team," he said.The 36-year-old credited his work in the nets for helping him rediscover his touch after a difficult run through the ODI series and the first Test."I think I just haven't had any rhythm, to be honest with you. I kind of struggled with rhythm through the ODI series, even coming up to the first Test. So I think it was just a case of just trying to find a feeling.It can be a bit tricky when you haven't played for months. Yeah, I was just trying to go into the nets and just trying to find the feeling that I kind of had last year," Bavuma said.Bavuma's innings was supported by Marco Jansen 's 85 and Simon Harmer 's 82, with the latter adding 183 runs with the captain. Praising their contributions, Bavuma said both batters played important roles in turning the innings around."Very brave innings from him," Bavuma said of Jansen, while he praised Harmer for showing "a lot of application" and felt the all-rounder was unlucky to miss out on a century.With South Africa having fought back into the contest, Bavuma said the batting unit had done its part and the responsibility now rested with the bowlers.
Article Summary: South Africa captain Temba Bavuma reveals how Sachin Tendulkar influenced his technique. Bavuma made a career-best 179 against Australia in the second Test at St George's Park. The 36-year-old helped South Africa recover from 110/6 to post 425/9 declared.

Article Title: No sponsor, a career-threatening setback and one big dream: Nayanika Sanga’s story
Article Text:
Nayanika Sanga (Insta)

NEW DELHI:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

For Nayanika Sanga, golf has always been about more than the scorecard. As the 22-year-old from Gurugram prepares to compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram, she is drawing on lessons learnt over years of competition, international exposure and a difficult comeback from injury. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.The philosophy reflects a maturity that has developed through experience. Having travelled abroad for tournaments, including competing in France, Nayanika has learnt to approach the demands of professional golf with greater perspective.“When you play in India, it is like a family. You feel at home and at ease. But when you play outside, the environment is different. People are new, and there can be a language barrier. I think that has made me a little more resilient. When I compete back home now, I feel comfortable because I know the place and the people,” she said.Her journey began when she was five. Her father, who serves in the Navy, wanted her to take up a sport, believing it would help her develop as an individual. She tried squash, tennis and golf, but the response to her natural ability with a club encouraged the family to pursue the latter.Competition soon followed, and the game became a defining part of her life.One of the earliest milestones arrived when she was 11, winning the Kazi Cup at Willingdon Club in Mumbai.“That was definitely a life-changing experience because that was my first win as a child, a big win as a child. Once you start winning, it reinforces that feeling that you want to keep chasing it again and again,” she said.The road since then, however, has not been without setbacks. A wrist injury four years ago came at a particularly difficult time, when she had just turned professional and was playing well. Gratitude journalling became an important part of that process.“When I started playing again, I began focusing on smaller things and feeling grateful that at least today I can play, and tomorrow I can compete. Instead of thinking, ‘I need to win today’, being grateful for the small things in life has definitely helped me,” she said.Physical conditioning has also played a significant role in her return. A professional golfer’s workload extends beyond the hours spent practising and playing. Frequent travel, tournaments scheduled close together and the physical demands of carrying her own bag at overseas events can take a toll. Nayanika credits her strength and conditioning coach, Shaurya Sinha, with helping her rebuild confidence in her body and handle the demands of the circuit.“Because of fitness, I have been a little more resilient to injuries. Other than the injury I had four years ago, I have not had any issues, and I feel my fitness routine is what gets me going every week,” she said.The Women’s Indian Open will present another test. Nayanika regards the DLF Golf and Country Club course as challenging, but prefers to see its demands as an opportunity rather than an obstacle.“I think it is challenging in a fun way. I do not see the course as challenging; rather, every day will be a new challenge there. It will be fun to tackle a new challenge every day,” she said.That outlook also shapes how she approaches a field featuring accomplished players. Rather than becoming preoccupied with the reputations of her opponents, she wants to learn from them while remaining focused on her own performance. She relies more on feel and instinct than data when making decisions on the course, trusting her judgement when she believes her game is in good shape.Nayanika has also witnessed the growth of women’s golf in India. When she first turned professional, she recalled fields of around 30 to 35 players. This year, she said, the numbers have risen to approximately 60 to 62, reflecting greater interest among younger golfers in pursuing the professional route. Lower scores and more opportunities to compete overseas have contributed to the improving standard.Yet the growth of the game has not removed one of its persistent challenges: funding. Despite competing abroad and continuing to develop as a professional, she is still looking for a sponsor. Coming from a middle-class family, with her father serving in the Navy, she knows the financial demands of sustaining a career on tour.“It has been tough. My parents have sacrificed so much for me, and they continue to do so to support me,” she said.Her grandparents also travelled with her to tournaments when she was younger, stepping in whenever her father’s work commitments prevented him from accompanying her. Nayanika acknowledges their contribution.Away from golf, time with friends and playing badminton help her switch off from the constant demands of professional competition. She also looks up to Diksha Dagar and Aditi Ashok whose achievements have out Indian golf on the global map.Nayanika hopes her journey can encourage more young girls to pursue sport, particularly in a society where conventional career choices often dominate expectations.“If you fall in love with a sport, there is nothing better than that feeling. Parents should be willing to explore sporting opportunities when their children show interest and ability,” she said.As she heads into the Women’s Indian Open, her ambitions remain tied to the fundamentals she has learnt through experience: trust her instincts, stay patient and focus on the next shot. For a golfer who has learnt to find perspective in adversity, the challenge is not simply to compete against a strong field, but to keep moving forward, one round at a time.
Article Summary: Nayanika Sanga, 22, will compete at the Women’s Indian Open from Oct 22-25 at the DLF Golf and Country Club in Gurugram. Her approach is simple: concentrate on what she can control, appreciate the opportunity to play and treat every round as a fresh challenge.

Article Title: Three Jharkhand players in India squad for historic lawn bowls series against New Zealand
Article Text:
(From left) Sunil Bahadur, Dinesh Kumar and Reshma Kumari

Kolkata: Three players from Jharkhand will be part of India’s four-member lawn bowls squad for a historic three-Test series against New Zealand in Nov, part of the centenary celebrations of sporting ties between the two countries.Lawn bowls is one of the only four sports, alongside cricket, hockey and football, selected for the centenary programme.2022 Commonwealth Games silver medallists Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur and rising player Reshma Kumari, all from Jharkhand, have been selected alongside Arjuna Awardee and Commonwealth Games gold medallist Pinki Singh for the series, scheduled from Nov 16-18 in Auckland.“This is a very important event for us because only four sports are taking part in the centenary celebrations. Yet another tale of administrative chaos and athletes paying the price. Caught in a prolonged governance crisis at the Equestrian Federation of India (EFI), Indian riders now face a ban from international competitions, with their sporting futures hanging in the balance. The latest setback comes at a time when the govt is pushing to bring more international events to India and widen Indian athletes’ exposure to global competition.The International Equestrian Federation (FEI) has decided to suspend the EFI from Dec 1 over prolonged governance irregularities and failure to hold fresh elections, effectively shutting Indian riders, officials, trainers and horses out of international events. TOI is in possession of FEI’s Oct 15 letter confirming the decision, which was taken at the international body's board meeting on Oct 13.Explaining its move, the FEI said the EFI’s prolonged governance crisis had reached a tipping point. “The absence of elections to date to elect a new Executive Committee, has resulted in a prolonged governance and leadership irregularity that is no longer sustainable,” the letter by FEI Governance Director Francisco Lima stated.The crisis follows the Delhi high court’s dissolution of the EFI executive committee in Feb 2026. Its elected tenure had expired in Sept 2023, while fresh elections remain pending nine months after the court’s intervention. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) constituted an ad hoc committee on March 27 to oversee the federation and facilitate the electoral process.While acknowledging the committee’s Sept 27 submission and its work, the FEI said elections were expected by Jan 31, 2027. However, the suspension will be reviewed only after the polls are held and evaluated by the international body.The consequences are sweeping. Citing its statutes, the FEI said the EFI “may not attend or be represented at any session or meeting of any FEI body, nor may it organise international events.” More damagingly, athletes, officials, trainers and horses “may not participate in international events organised by the FEI or any other national federation, whether under the Indian flag or the FEI flag.”With the suspension taking effect before the stated election deadline, Indian riders risk losing crucial international competition opportunities. Their return will depend on the completion of elections and the FEI’s subsequent evaluation, leaving athletes caught in a governance crisis they did not create.

Former Australia captain Steve Smith has been cleared of concussion and resumed fielding duties on the fifth day of the first Test against South Africa at Kingsmead in Durban on Tuesday, after undergoing a series of clinical assessments following a blow to the helmet.The 37-year-old batter was struck by a short-pitched delivery from Anrich Nortje during Australia's second innings. Smith attempted to duck under the ball but misjudged its trajectory as it failed to rise as much as he expected.Although he continued batting after the incident, scoring 27 off 41 balls before being caught at long-on off Simon Harmer, Smith did not take the field when South Africa began their second innings on Monday. Michael Neser served as his substitute fielder during that session.However, Smith returned to the field on Tuesday morning after being cleared under Cricket Australia's concussion protocols. He was stationed in the slip cordon when South Africa resumed their chase and subsequently took a catch to dismiss Kyle Verreynne off Matt Renshaw's bowling."Steve Smith has undergone a series of clinical assessments over the past 24 hours in accordance with Cricket Australia’s concussion protocols and has been cleared to take the field this morning," Cricket Australia said in a statement.The incident brought back memories of Smith's previous concussion scare during the 2019 Ashes in England, when he was struck on the head by fast bowler Jofra Archer and forced to miss part of a Test match.Smith's return to the field came after medical assessments over the preceding 24 hours, with Australia following the prescribed protocols before allowing the experienced batter to resume his duties.His presence was a boost for Australia as they pushed for victory in the series opener, with South Africa mounting a determined resistance on the final day.South Africa resumed at 102/4 on Tuesday, needing another 319 runs to win. They reached 166/6 by lunch after Australia struck twice to strengthen their grip on the contest.Opener Aiden Markram led the home side's resistance, remaining unbeaten on 69 at the interval alongside Marco Jansen on seven. It’s been barely 48 hours since India landed in Christchurch after taking a flight out of Bengaluru. Shreyas Iyer and his men will be forgiven for still being sleep-deprived and jet-lagged when they walk out at Hagley Oval for the first of five T20Is against New Zealand today. Indian cricketers are conditioned to relentless travel, but that does not make the grind any less demanding. The modern cricket calendar is shaped more by commercial interests and diplomatic necessities and less by sporting logic and priorities. This tour is a case study.Stretching over 43 days, the visit marks a century of sporting ties between India and New Zealand, a relationship that dates back to the great Major Dhyan Chand leading an Indian Army hockey team to the country in 1926. It also offers New Zealand crowds a rare chance to watch Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma when the five-match ODI series follows the T20Is from Nov 4.Beyond all the ceremonial details, the tour could provide clues about the direction that Indian cricket takes across the three formats. For the Indian cricket fan and an unforgiving media, large sections of which are digital, the strains of a packed schedule are rarely considered valid excuses for a dip in performance standards and middling results.One saw that during the difficult tours of Ireland and England earlier this year.For many fans, critics and pundits, a side that can win two successive World Cups in a fickle format like T20, just cannot lose. While the Test team has got a good chance to acclimatise, the T20I side has been on the treadmill, playing non-stop in different conditions and continents. Predictably, skipper Iyer downplayed the scheduling challenge.“We’ve done that in the past... It’s fun at the same time to be travelling, playing and getting accustomed to new conditions. We just want to put the reasons aside and see how we plan to win,” he said on match-eve.The coming 10 days could prove revealing for both the captain and his team. India’s T20 setup remains in transition, with the road ultimately leading to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics and the T20 World Cup in Australia and New Zealand later that year. While the composition of the touring squads suggests the two-Test series remains a priority, the T20 side arrives carrying a degree of desperation. That was reflected in the decision to recall Bhuvneshwar Kumar Discarded after the 2022 New Zealand tour, the veteran seamer, now nearing 37, has been drafted in to lend experience to a bowling attack that is still searching for options in the absence of the peerless Jasprit Bumrah “Bhuvi brings a lot of experience. We were lacking that... He has won the IPL in the last two years and knows how to dominate this format,” Iyer explained.The bigger question is whether India have done enough over the last two years to build bowling depth beyond Bumrah. Bhuvneshwar’s return can be looked at with a mixed lens. Yes, it is a vote of confidence in a trusted campaigner. Under Gautam Gambhir and the current selection panel, India largely embraced a perform-or-perish approach, often showing limited patience with senior players.The recall of Bhuvneshwar therefore feels like a tactical retreat, an attempt to steady a T20 ship that rocked violently during the UK tour earlier this year. Whether this small step back helps India take a significant leap forward is a question only the next fortnight can answer.

BENGALURU: Home advantage is losing its sheen in international cricket, with teams increasingly equipped to beat opponents in the latter's own backyard. Former head coach Gary Stead believes hosts New Zealand may not enjoy the edge they once did when India begin their tour with the T20 series beginning on Thursday, with the visitors’ improved pace attack and the ability to adapt to challenging conditions making them a formidable opponent.The 54-year-old, who oversaw a successful phase in New Zealand cricket, including their World Test Championship triumph, said the days of exploiting an opponent’s perceived weakness were fading.“Earlier, you played India and thought, ‘Oh, we’ll do a green track because they don’t have good seamers.’ Now they have quality seamers as well,” Stead said.Referring to New Zealand’s 3-0 triumph in the 2024 Test series in India, he added: “The same way, when we came in 2024, we had quality spinners too. The whole idea of home advantage has disappeared a little bit around the world. Everyone has shown the competence to beat everyone else at any given time. So you’ve got to be on your game and be sharp.”Stead, currently head coach of Andhra’s Ranji Trophy team, believes India’s ability to adapt to New Zealand’s bouncy surfaces will be crucial to their chances.“The Indians are going to have to adapt to bouncy wickets, some of the bounciest possibly in the world.The wickets will have bounce and carry. If the Indian players can nullify New Zealand’s bowlers, then I think it’ll be a cracking series,” he said.The Test matches, in particular, could pose the toughest challenge. Stead pointed to Hagley Oval in Christchurch and Basin Reserve Wellington as venues traditionally known for their extra bounce.“It's very important for New Zealand. India are obviously an amazing Test side, and then we go to Australia and play, so there are six huge Tests coming up for New Zealand. But if you want to be judged against the best, you’ve got to compete against the best as well,” he said.With Australia and South Africa also producing compelling Test cricket recently, Stead believes the influence of T20 cricket is increasingly visible in the longest format.“I think the T20 format has allowed players a little bit more freedom in the way they play. And I think that’s rubbing off on Test cricket now as well,” he said.Stead also called on the International Cricket Council (ICC) to explore more multi-format series, arguing that longer tours could help sustain interest across formats.“Personally, I think the ICC should consider playing more multi-format series. Rather than teams coming and going very quickly and people forgetting about the series, it could be a little like the women’s Ashes, where they have multi-format scenarios. I really think it’s something that could take off,” he said.However, he acknowledged that fitting longer tours into an increasingly crowded international calendar would be difficult, with teams constantly preparing for the next World Cup in one of the two white-ball formats.

By the time the final Odisha wicket tumbled at the Greenfield Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram on Wednesday afternoon, the hosts had notched up an innings win with seven vital points on their home turf. Kerala needed a little over 23 overs to wrap up Odisha’s innings for 143 and register an innings and 36-run win.At the centre was Jalaj Saxena , the veteran off-spinner, who mesmerised Odisha with his bagful of tricks to finish with figures of 5/34 from 18 overs.This was Jalaj’s 35th five-wicket haul in the Ranji Trophy , a phenomenal number that puts him level with the great Bishan Singh Bedi for the joint fifth-most five-fors in the tournament’s history. Odisha, meanwhile, became the 20th Ranji team he has taken five wickets against.Quiz him on his record-breaking day, though, and the man shrugs. “I didn’t know about equalling Bishan paaji,” he says. “Who is the bowler with the highest five-fors? Is it Rajinder Goel?” he asks. Jalaj is correct.The legendary slow-left-arm orthodox spinner holds the record for the most five-wicket hauls in the Ranji Trophy, with 59 five-fors.The recipe for Jalaj’s success is built on his love for the game. “I just love the feeling of putting on the whites and playing for four days,” Jalaj tells TOI.In the offseason, he worked tirelessly on his fitness, assiduously strengthening his back and core to build stamina for bowling longer spells.“Odisha was already on the backfoot and were four wickets down coming into the final day. The plan was simple: land the ball in the right areas,” he explains.Jalaj landed the ball in the right areas, and the pitch did the rest. Like a true team man, Jalaj credits the group and not himself for this resounding win. “It is a team effort,” he says.The platform was set by Kerala’s batters, with centuries from Sachin Baby and Mohammed Azharuddeen.At 39, the age when most cricketers walk into the sunset, Jalaj is hungry and still looks to climb the ladder. “If you don’t have long-term goals, then there is no point in playing Ranji Trophy,” he quips. “Progressing to the next level is what I always aspire to,” he elaborates.“If you ask Sachin and Azhar, even they have aspirations of playing in the IPL and representing India,” Jalaj explains.His never-say-die attitude could rub off on some of Kerala’s younger players. Among them is off-spinner Vaisakh Chandran, who made a comeback to first-class cricket in the previous game against Jharkhand.“I love bowling in tandem with Vaisakh. He is a talented off-spinner and a keen learner,” he adds.The timing makes this win sweeter. With the festival in the air, Saxena has delivered the perfect Dussehra gift for Kerala. Next up is Bengal. “Taking it one game at a time. Not looking too far ahead,” Jalaj concludes.
Article Summary: Kerala beat Odisha by an innings and 36 runs in the Ranji Trophy. Jalaj Saxena took figures of 5/34 from 18 overs. It was his 35th five-wicket haul in the tournament. He is level with Bishan Singh Bedi for fifth-most five-fors.

Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Jalaj Saxena's five-for powers Kerala to innings win over Odisha; Mumbai notch second bonus-point victory

Veteran all-rounder Jalaj Saxena took five wickets as Kerala bowled Odisha out for 143 in their second innings to secure an innings and 36-run victory in their Ranji Trophy Elite Group C match in Thiruvananthapuram on Wednesday.The win took Kerala to third place in the standings, behind Maharashtra and Bengal. Bengal had beaten Services by 60 runs on Tuesday.Asked to follow on, Odisha resumed their second innings at 102/4 but lost their remaining six wickets for just 41 runs. They were bowled out for 143 in 58.3 overs, allowing Kerala to seal the win in the second session on the fourth and final day.Saxena led the attack with figures of 5/34 in 18 overs, including seven maidens. Odisha could not build on their overnight score, with their final two wickets falling to run-outs.Opener Gourav Choudhary top-scored with 53, while captain Subhranshu Senapati made 30. The pair had helped Odisha recover from early setbacks before Saxena took apart the lower order.Odisha had scored 225 in their first innings, giving Kerala a lead of 179 after the hosts posted 404. Mohammed Azharuddeen was named Player of the Match for his unbeaten 139 in Kerala's first innings.Delhi bounced back from their opening-round defeat to Bengal by earning three points against Gujarat at Palam B Ground. The match ended in a draw, with Delhi gaining the points on the basis of their first-innings lead.Delhi's first-innings total of 648/6 declared proved decisive. Ayush Badoni scored 217, while Priyansh Arya made 199 off 221 balls. Arya was named Player of the Match for his innings.Gujarat, who had topped the standings after the first round, resumed their first innings at 363/5 on the final day. They added 116 runs before being bowled out for 479 in 174.1 overs.Manan Hingrajia, who was unbeaten on 108 overnight, went on to score 123 off 303 balls. Captain Chintan Gaja also extended his overnight score of 41 to 82, but Gujarat still conceded a first-innings deficit of 169 runs.Delhi's Hrithik Shokeen took five wickets for 143 runs, while Sumit Mathur claimed two. Delhi enforced the follow-on, and Gujarat reached 15/1 in eight overs in their second innings before the match was drawn.Delhi earned three points to move to sixth place in the eight-team standings, while Gujarat collected one point.Punjab's spinners Harjas Singh and Emanjot Singh Chahal took three wickets each to help their team beat Chhattisgarh by seven wickets in their Group B Ranji Trophy match in Mullanpur on Wednesday.After scoring 456 in their first innings, Punjab bowled Chhattisgarh out for 206 and enforced the follow-on. The visitors put up a stronger fight in their second innings, scoring 335, but that left Punjab with a target of just 86 runs.Punjab completed the chase in 16.5 overs, losing three wickets on the way to victory.Hyderabad secured a 267-run victory over Andhra in Mulapadu. Left-arm spinner Tanay Thyagarajan took six wickets for 35 runs on the final day as Andhra were bowled out for 130.Saurashtra earned three points against Karnataka in Alur after taking a narrow first-innings lead. It was the second consecutive match in which Saurashtra finished with three points.Karnataka declared their second innings at 243/7, setting Saurashtra a target of 237. With limited time left in the match, Saurashtra chose to secure the points rather than push for an outright win.Saurashtra finished at 137/2 in their second innings, with Chirag Jani unbeaten on 63 off 117 balls.Mumbai recorded their second consecutive bonus-point victory in the Ranji Trophy Elite Group D, beating Himachal Pradesh by an innings and 97 runs in Bilaspur on Wednesday.Mumbai declared their first innings at 528/8, with Sarfaraz Khan scoring 154 and Akash Anand making 117. Article Title: Ranji Trophy: Railways spoil Rajasthan’s victory push with gritty draw
Article Text:
Ajay Kukna

JAIPUR: Echoing the outcome of their opening fixture against Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan once again settled for three points as their Ranji Trophy Group ‘D’ match against Railways ended in a draw at the Sawai Man Singh Stadium here on Wednesday, securing the advantage courtesy of a first-innings lead. Rajasthan's hopes of pressing for an outright victory were hampered by injuries to key bowlers. Pacer Akash Singh hurt his right hand while completing a caught-and-bowled dismissal of Mohammad Saif in the first innings, while left-arm spinner Ajay Kukna developed finger swelling, leaving him unable to bowl at full capacity.Resuming the final morning at 305/6, Railways folded within the first hour to finish their first innings at 338. Kukna emerged as the standout bowler with figures of 4 for 106, a stellar spell that earned him appreciation even from the opposition camp.Acknowledging his threat, Railways centurion Saif, who struck 103 not out off 118 balls (8x4, 4x6), said, “This pitch wasn’t really an outright result wicket and no bowler was that difficult to play. But I would specially praise Kukna, because taking five wickets in the last match and four wickets here is no easy feat.He puts a good loop on the ball.”Having restricted the visitors, Rajasthan enforced the follow-on. Railways quickly lost both openers when they came out to bat again in a hectic first session that saw six wickets tumble across the morning action, the only window where the bowlers extracted life from the surface. However, that early flurry proved to be the last twist in the tale.Any hopes Rajasthan harboured of forcing an outright victory on the placid track were firmly dashed by a third-wicket partnership of unbeaten 155, compounded further by the team's young and inexperienced bowling attack.Rajasthan captain Kartik Sharma acknowledged the team’s inability to extract wickets. “The plan was to get them out quickly and enforce the follow-on, and that's exactly what happened. But later on, wickets stopped coming. Plus, our bowlers Akash and Kukna got injured. Hopefully, Kukna will recover by the next match and we will know about Akash's status soon,” he added.Eshaan Goyal and Saif dug their heels in, frustrating the hosts through the remainder of the day. Goyal provided a watchful anchor with an undefeated 59 off 132 deliveries.With the surface giving bowlers virtually no room to maneuver, the match meandered to a tame draw as Railways safely reached 176/2 in their second innings when stumps were drawn.The Rajasthan captain backed his young pace attack, saying, “First of all, our bowling attack is not weak. And, we have to introduce young players into the side eventually, so we are looking ahead and building them. They need to be prepared and gain experience, and this is the exact time for our young bowlers to gain that exposure,” he explained.Rajasthan will next take on Uttarakhand in Dehradun from October 26.
Article Summary: Rajasthan's hopes of pressing for an outright victory were hampered by injuries to key bowlers. Pacer Akash Singh hurt his right hand while completing a caught- and-bowled dismissal of Mohammad Saif in the first innings. Left-arm spinner Ajay Kukna developed finger swelling, leaving him unable to bowl at full capacity.

Australian batting superstar Steve Smith reached another career milestone on Wednesday, becoming the third Australian and the 12th player overall to score 11,000 runs in Test cricket during the second Test against South Africa in Gqeberha.The 37-year-old achieved the landmark during Australia's first innings at St George's Park, scoring 28 off 88 balls, including two fours, before being bowled by Wiaan Mulder.Smith reached 11,000 Test runs in 226 innings, making him the fifth-fastest batter to the milestone. Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara holds the record, having taken just 208 innings, followed by West Indies great Brian Lara (213).Smith joined former Australia captains Ricky Ponting and Allan Border in the country's exclusive 11,000-run club. Ponting tops the Australian list with 13,378 Test runs, while Border finished his career with 11,174.Among batters to reach the milestone, Ponting needed 222 innings, while India's Sachin Tendulkar took 223. Smith's 226 innings put him ahead of Rahul Dravid and South Africa's Jacques Kallis, who both required 234 innings.The landmark adds to Smith's remarkable record in the longest format, where he has established himself as one of the leading batters of his generation.Smith's personal achievement came on a difficult day for Australia, who were dismissed for just 99 in their first innings after South Africa posted a commanding total.Marco Jansen led the hosts' attack with five wickets, while Mulder claimed two, including Smith's wicket.South Africa's innings was anchored by captain Temba Bavuma, who scored 179, with Jansen contributing 85 to help the hosts recover from an early collapse.Having secured a substantial first-innings advantage, South Africa enforced the follow-on and put Australia under immense pressure in the ongoing second Test of the series.
Article Summary: Steve Smith becomes the 12th player to score 11,000 runs in Test cricket. The 37-year-old reached the landmark during Australia's first innings at St George's Park. He scored 28 off 88 balls, including two fours, before being bowled by Wiaan Mulder. Sri Lanka's Kumar Sangakkara holds the record, having taken just 208 innings.

Delhi Capitals (DC) have appointed former India spinner Amit Mishra as their spin bowling coach ahead of the Indian Premier League (IPL) 2027 season. Mishra, who played 162 IPL matches for four franchises, will take up a coaching role in the tournament for the first time after retiring from professional cricket last September.Mishra represented Delhi Daredevils (now Delhi Capitals), Deccan Chargers, Sunrisers Hyderabad and Lucknow Super Giants during his IPL career."The OG Tiger has returned! Amit Mishra, our highest ever wicket-taker, is now our spin-bowling coach," DC wrote in a post on X.Mishra is among the leading wicket-takers in IPL history, with 174 wickets from 162 matches. He also holds the record for the most hat-tricks in the tournament, having taken three during his career."A tiger is the one who never leaves his prey. Dilli is my heartbeat. We will try to give the happiness to the Dilli fans, which they have been waiting for these many years," Mishra said in a video posted on the franchise's social media handles on Wednesday.Delhi Capitals finished sixth in the 2026 season and are yet to win an IPL title. Mishra's IPL career began in 2008, when he took a five-wicket haul in his first match. That performance included the first of his three hat-tricks in the tournament.He took his other two hat-tricks in 2011 and 2013. No bowler has taken more hat-tricks in the league's history than Mishra, who represented Haryana in domestic cricket.Known for his flighted leg-breaks, Mishra played in every IPL season from 2008 to 2024 except 2022. He played his last IPL match for Lucknow Super Giants in 2024 and finished his career in the tournament with 174 wickets at an economy rate of 7.37.Mishra represented India across all three formats between 2003 and 2017. He played 22 Tests, 36 ODIs and 10 T20Is for the country.
Article Summary: Former India spinner Amit Mishra appointed spin bowling coach for Delhi Capitals. Mishra played 162 IPL matches for four franchises. He holds the record for the most hat-tricks in the tournament, having taken three during his career. Delhi Capitals are yet to win an IPL title.

Article Title: Ishan Kishan on the verge of three major T20 records as India take on New Zealand

Can Kishan become India's first 2,000-run batter in a year?

NEW DELHI: Ishan Kishan has three major batting milestones in sight as India prepare for the five-match T20I series against New Zealand, starting in Christchurch on Thursday. The wicketkeeper-batter is closing in on the record for most T20I runs by an Indian in a calendar year, the overall record for a batter from a Test-playing nation and the landmark of 2,000 runs in T20 cricket in a single year.Kishan, who has enjoyed a breakthrough year in India's T20I setup, needs just seven runs to surpass Suryakumar Yadav 's Indian record of 1,164 T20I runs in a calendar year, achieved in 2022.The left-hander has scored 1,158 runs in 34 T20I innings this year at an average of 37.35 and a strike rate of 172.06, including a century and seven half-centuries.Kishan is also closing in on the calendar-year record for most T20I runs by a batter from a Test-playing nation. Pakistan's Mohammad Rizwan holds the mark with 1,326 runs in 2021, leaving Kishan 139 runs short of the milestone.The India batter is also just 46 runs away from becoming the seventh Indian to complete 2,000 runs in T20Is. In 66 matches, he has scored 1,954 runs at an average of 31.51 and a strike rate of 148.81, with one century and 13 half-centuries.Beyond international cricket, Kishan has another significant milestone within reach.He has scored 1,760 runs in 49 T20 matches this year at an average of 38.26 and a strike rate above 175.He needs another 240 runs to become the first Indian batter to score 2,000 runs in T20 cricket in a calendar year. West Indies' Nicholas Pooran and Rizwan are the only batters to have crossed that mark, with Pooran scoring 2,331 runs in 2024 and Rizwan accumulating 2,036 in 2021.With five T20Is against New Zealand followed by a three-match series against Sri Lanka in December, Kishan has opportunities to rewrite the record books before the year ends.
Article Summary: Ishan Kishan chasing three major batting milestones in 2013. Wicketkeeper-batter is closing in on record for most T20I runs by an Indian in a calendar year, the overall record for a batter from a Test-playing nation and the landmark of 2,000 runs in T20 cricket in a single year.

India’s Suvarna Raj won the gold medal in the women’s F54 discus throw at the Asian Para Games on Thursday. She topped the event with a best throw of 15.66m.Suvarna put up a strong show, crossing the 15m mark four times in her six attempts. Article Title: Sexual offence charge rocks India's Asian Para Games contingent; swimmer faces lifetime ban
Article Text:
Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh (Image credit: Instagram)

NEW DELHI: The Indian contingent at the Asian Para Games in Nagoya has been left embarrassed after para swimmer Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh was detained by Japanese police following allegations of sexually harassing and molesting a female hotel employee. The 40-year-old, once a world No 1 in his event, was sent back to India on Tuesday, a day after the alleged incident, and faces the prospect of a lifetime ban from the Paralympic Committee of India (PCI).A senior PCI official, who is part of the Indian delegation in Nagoya and who handled the entire situation, confirmed the development to TOI, describing the alleged misconduct as “reprehensible and intolerable” and saying there could be “no justification” for such behaviour by an athlete representing the country on the international stage.”“Aalam is staring at no less than a lifetime ban for bringing disrepute to the entire Indian delegation participating at the Asian Para Games and for embarrassing the country on the world stage,” the official said.According to the official, the incident occurred on Monday at the Four Points by Sheraton hotel, where the Indian para swimming team was staying. The female employee was reportedly carrying out housekeeping duties in the swimmer’s room when the alleged misconduct took place.“The local organising committee (LOC) informed the chef-de-mission’s (CDM) office that an alleged sexual harassment and molestation incident had occurred at the hotel and that an Indian athlete had been detained by the local police,” the official said.“When we reached the hotel, the police and senior hotel managers were already there. We were told that the athlete had inappropriately touched the female housekeeping staff member, made sexually coloured gestures, attempted to grope her and made sexual advances. She rushed out and informed her superiors. This is what we were told by the police and hotel staff,” the official added.The official said the delegation apologised to the hotel authorities and the employee. Following the complaint, police detained Shaikh and took him to a local police station. The official said the authorities sought his arrest and that he be formally presented before a court.The LOC subsequently intervened, with the Indian delegation asked to furnish a written apology to the employee and ensure that the athlete left Japan. Shaikh was moved to another hotel for the night and booked on the first available flight, departing Nagoya at around 2 pm local time on Tuesday, the official said. He was released after the written apology was furnished, according to the official’s account.“The police authorities had clearly recorded the sexual offence allegation in their formal complaint, in Japanese. We can confirm that since I saw that,” the official said.The official added the incident had diverted senior Indian officials from the contingent’s ongoing sporting campaign. “Instead of focusing on the Games and our athletes’ performances, we spent several hours at the police station and later at the hotel premises convincing the authorities. We were embarrassed in front of everyone,” the official said.He added that the employee appeared to be in deep shock when the delegation returned to the hotel. The hotel and LOC, he said, sought updates on the action India would take and warned that they could pursue formal legal proceedings if they were dissatisfied with the response.The PCI has informed the govt in New Delhi of the proposed action, the official said. After the Games, PCI officials, para swimming administrators and members of the delegation will deliberate on the matter and recommend stringent sanctions to the sports ministry and Sports Authority of India (SAI).“The CDM’s office has already recommended a lifetime ban. A formal decision will be taken at a meeting in Delhi after we return,” the official said.Shaikh, who hails from Bihar’s Madhubani district and lives with his family in Mumbai’s Dharavi, was sent home without competing in his scheduled events on Wednesday.A former world No. 1 in the men’s 100m butterfly (S5) and 50m breaststroke (SB4), according to World Para Swimming records, Shaikh represented India at the 2018 Asian Para Games in Jakarta and won 200m breaststroke gold at the Reykjavik International Games last year, setting Indian and Asian records.The incident comes close on the heels of an Indian hockey umpire and technical official Gurinder Singh Sangha was being sent home from the able-bodied Asian Games in Nagoya following sexual misconduct and harassment complaints by a Malaysian hockey official and a hotel staff member.
Article Summary: Para swimmer Mohammad Shams Aalam Shaikh was detained by Japanese police following allegations of sexually harassing and molesting a female hotel employee. The 40-year-old, once a world No 1 in his event, was sent back to India on Tuesday, a day after the alleged incident. Shaikh faces the prospect of a lifetime ban from the Paralympic Committee of India.

Article Title: Asian Para Games 2026: Bhavina Patel, Subham Wadhwa win bronze in mixed doubles table tennis
Article Text:
Subham Wadhwa and Bhavina Patel (Image credit: X)

How Bhavina and Subham reached the semifinals

What are the XD7 and XD17 categories?

India’s Bhavina Patel and Subham Wadhwa finished with a bronze medal in mixed doubles table tennis at the Asian Para Games on Thursday. The Indian pair lost to South Korea’s Jang Yeongjin and Lee Migyu in the XD7 semifinal.Bhavina and Subham went down 6-11, 11-8, 5-11, 8-11. However, their place on the podium had already been confirmed after they reached the last four.The Indian pair produced a strong performance in the quarterfinals to beat Japan’s Kimie Bessho and Masanori Uno in straight games. They won the match 11-9, 11-3, 11-6 to secure their place in the semifinals and guarantee themselves a medal.However, they could not overcome the South Korean pair in the next round and had to settle for bronze.India’s Dattaprasad Chougule and Savita also faced a tough finish in the mixed doubles XD17 event.The Indian pair won the first two games against the Philippines’ Wilfred Redulla and Manginsay Lhey, taking both 11-9. But their opponents fought back strongly to win the next three games 11-2, 11-6, 11-5.The 2-3 defeat ended the Indian pair’s campaign in the quarterfinals.In para table tennis, mixed doubles events are grouped according to the players’ physical impairments and classification. XD7 features wheelchair athletes with moderate sitting balance.XD17 generally features standing athletes with physical impairments affecting their legs and arms, from classes 6 to 10.
Article Summary: Bhavina Patel and Subham Wadhwa finished with a bronze medal in mixed doubles table tennis at the Asian Para Games. The Indian pair lost to South Korea’s Jang Yeongjin and Lee Migyu in the XD7 semifinal. Dattaprasad Chougule and Savita also lost in the mixed doubles XD17 event.

NEW DELHI: India returned to the top five of the Asian Para Games medal standings after another bumper day on Wednesday, adding 27 medals, including five gold, to take their overall tally to 62 after three days of competition in Aichi-Nagoya.After slipping to sixth despite winning 24 medals on Day 2, India leapfrogged Iran to claim fifth place, with 14 gold, 22 silver and 26 bronze medals. Athletics once again led the charge, accounting for 18 medals on Wednesday, including five gold, as India crossed the 50-medal mark comfortably.China continued to dominate the continental event, crossing the 100-gold mark and taking their overall tally to 226. Their 107 gold medals alone were more than second-placed Japan’s overall count of 100, underlining the hosts’ commanding lead.Japan occupied second place with 100 medals, while Uzbekistan slipped to third despite having the same 29 gold medals as the hosts. Japan’s superior silver and bronze counts kept them ahead. South Korea remained fourth with 46 medals, including 15 gold.India, Thailand and Iran had 14 gold medals apiece, with silver counts determining their positions in the standings. Thailand moved to sixth, pushing Iran, who were fifth after the second day, down to seventh.Kazakhstan, Indonesia and Iraq completed the top 10 after the third day.India’s 27-medal haul on Wednesday took their total from 35 after the first two days to 62. The five gold medals also brought the country’s gold tally to 14, keeping India firmly in contention for a strong overall finish.India’s athletics contingent delivered another outstanding performance, winning 18 medals, including five gold. Simran, Praveen Kumar and Sachin Khilari set new Games records, while Dilip Gavit and Ayush Verma also finished on top of the podium.Simran won the women’s 100m T12 gold in a Games-record time of 12.02 seconds, adding to her 200m title from Tuesday.
